name: coingecko-coin
title: Bitcoin Price: BTC/USD Live Price Chart, Market Cap & News Today | CoinGecko

knownGaps.why: Genuine limitation. One coin page runs from a $0.004683 tick to a $1.575T market cap — fifteen orders of magnitude in one document. The grid is set from the median (spot prices near $78,000, two decimals) and the per-amount significant-figure cap then pulls both ends off it: $0.004683 needs nine decimals not to read as zero, $1.575T has none left to spend.

Two separate things are red here and only one of them is a limitation.
(1) OPEN PRODUCT QUESTION: $1.575T renders as 2,019,230,769 ZEC. Total ZEC supply is 21 million, so every figure above that is arithmetic rather than a quantity anyone can hold — the number is arguably correct and certainly useless as a unit of account. Whether market caps should convert at all, render coarsely, or stay in fiat is undecided; recorded, not fixed.
(2) DEFECT, not a limitation: "$29.121B" renders as 37,334,615,385 ZEC, exactly 1000x too high. parseNumber in src/lib/detection/parser.ts reads the dot in "29.121" as thousands grouping because its US-decimal escape requires a single-digit integer part (sepIndex <= 1) — which is the only reason "$1.575T" on the same page comes out right. The unabbreviated sibling "$29,126,903,650" converts to 37,342,184 ZEC, which is what the abbreviated form should have shown.
